messages:
sara: Bringing up falcon-40b-int4 on the dedicated pool and running into OOMs when throughput > 40 rps for warm convo workloads. Batch size 2 fails on a few customer prompts with long histories. Anyone seen KV cache + fragmentation doing this?

kenji: yep, sounds familiar. falcon's KV blowup + int4 working set can fragment. what are your defaults for max_new_tokens and batch window? :thinking:

sara: current defaults: max_new_tokens=1024, batching.window_ms=25, batching.max_batch=8. The interesting bit: small requests are fine, but long-history chat with >1500 context tokens spikes memory then OOMs. Here's a crash log:```
E/serving: Allocation failed: unable to allocate 4.3GiB for backend KV cache
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
```

matt: immediate triage checklist: 1) lower max_new_tokens per-model default 2) enforce per-request token cap at route level 3) enable KV prefix eviction for large contexts

alex: agree. for this model we should try: max_new_tokens=512, batching.max_batch=4, batching.window_ms=10. also enable small-slab jemalloc config to reduce fragmentation. e.g. set MALLOC_CONF:
```
MALLOC_CONF=background_thread:true,dirty_decay_ms:15000,muzzy_decay_ms:15000,lg_chunk:20
```
should help reclaim.

kenji: also try soft-KV-eviction on prefix length > 1024: drop oldest kv entries for that session before adding new. we instrumented a similar fix on 13B and cut OOMs by ~80%.

sara: testing those now. quick config I'm pushing to the dedicated pool for model=falcon-40b-int4:
```json
{
  "model": "falcon-40b-int4",
  "defaults": {
    "max_new_tokens": 512,
    "batching": {"max_batch": 4, "window_ms": 10},
    "kv": {"prefix_eviction_threshold": 1024}
  }
}
```

deploy-bot: Rollout paused: new defaults for falcon-40b-int4 queued. Canary target: 10% of traffic on pool=falkirk-dedicated.

matt: one caution: lowering max_new_tokens may affect eval pass rates on our long-answer benchmark. add a targeted eval job comparing rouge/qa accuracy at 512 vs 1024 for the top 50 prompts. if quality regressions appear, we can autoscale capacity instead of increasing the token cap.

kenji: good call. also capture per-token latency distribution — smaller batches reduce tail spikes but raise per-token cost. we'll run cost/latency tradeoff for config sweep.

sara: quick test results after applying the config to canary (10 requests, mixed history lengths): 0 OOMs, p95 latency +7%, token cost +3%, qa-f1 on long answers down ~1.6 points. pushing broader canary then run the full eval.

alex: sounds reasonable. let's merge per-model defaults into model catalog so new deployments pick it up. also add a note in the model onboarding checklist: "check kv growth with long histories, tune max_new_tokens and enable prefix eviction".

matt: opened an eval job: https://redwood-internal/evals/runner/8943 — will post results when done.

sara: thanks all. if the full canary stays clean we set these as the default for falcon-40b-int4 and document the jemalloc tweak + kv eviction pattern in the bring-up playbook. :thumbsup:
